items.text: Getting into that better-paid tier takes more than a cloud certification, it takes one real, documented piece of infrastructure work and honesty about the on-call trade-off.

blocks.heading: Biggest Earners in Devops Actually Scale

items.text: A DevOps job can plateau exactly like any other job, a generalist pipeline-maintenance role at an IT-services firm has a real, fairly low ceiling.

Platform engineering, building the internal tooling that lets other developers self-serve deployments, is currently the fastest-growing DevOps-adjacent specialisation in Indian product and GCC hiring, and it pays a real premium over generalist pipeline maintenance.

An engineer who can cut a company's cloud bill by 20% with documented reasoning, or who owns a service's SLO and error budget end to end, is worth more than someone holding AWS, Azure, and three vendor badges with no real production ownership behind any of them.

blocks.heading: Need a CS Degree for This

items.text: The honest comparison is not "which credential sounds best." It is which route gets you to one real, provable piece of infrastructure work fastest, for the least unnecessary spend.
A strong foundation if you can get one, but genuinely not mandatory, DevOps is unusually open to people who prove skill through a home lab and real projects instead of a specific degree name.
Fully viable.

blocks.heading: Devops Engineer: Owns the Delivery Lifecycle End

items.text: Platform engineer: builds the internal tooling and self-service platform other engineers use to ship without needing DevOps hand-holding for every deploy.

A live incident is a genuinely different kind of pressure than a missed deadline, it is time-boxed, often visible to leadership in real time, and can carry blame dynamics that other engineering work does not.

The tool surface is wide by design, Linux, networking, one or two clouds, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD, observability, which creates a real risk of staying shallow across many tools instead of building depth in one.
Routine log analysis and first-pass alert correlation, AI-assisted observability tools now triage a large share of the noisy, low-value alerts that used to eat a DevOps engineer's morning.
Boilerplate script and pipeline-config generation, tools like GitHub Copilot speed up writing a Terraform module or a CI/CD YAML file from a known pattern.
First-draft infrastructure documentation and incident-summary write-ups, the repetitive documentation work that historically got skipped under deadline pressure.
